panel.summary: Legacy `GET /images/:id` is unauthenticated, and it is the endpoint the PPTX/DOCX import path uploads to — imported deck images are world-readable
panel.evidence: `ImageController.get` carries no `@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)` and no workspace scoping (image.controller.ts:44-53), unlike the v1 controller which guards with `CombinedAuthGuard, WorkspaceScopeGuard` and prefixes the S3 key with the workspace id (packages/backend/src/api/v1/images.controller.ts:24, 78-97). The frontend PPTX import path uploads every embedded image through `docsImageUploader` → `POST ${BACKEND_BASE}/images` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:31, used by packages/frontend/src/app/slides/pptx-actions.ts:39), i.e. into the UNSCOPED, publicly readable bucket root. Anyone who obtains or brute-scans an image URL (returned as `/images/<uuid>.<ext>`) can read confidential imported slide/document artwork with no session at all. Confidence is low because UUIDv4 keys make this a capability-URL design that may be intentional — but the REST docs touched by this change (developers/rest-api.md:124) describe images as "workspace-scoped", which this endpoint is not.
panel.finding_key: packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts::legacy `get /images/:id` is unauthenticated, and it is the endpoint the pptx/docx import path uploads to — imported deck images are world-readable
